title: Crypto losses continue as inflation persists; portfolio value falls to $60,200
paragraphs: Bitcoin traded near $67,253, down 2.9% over 24 hours, while ether fell 2.5% to about $1,905. The broader crypto market lost 3.5% of its value, leaving total capitalization near $2.34 trillion, according to CoinGecko. Weekly losses were deeper: 11.5% for bitcoin and 15% for ether. The decline remains broad, with persistent inflation adding a difficult backdrop for assets sensitive to interest rates and investor appetite for risk.

US producer prices rose 0.3% in October, slowing from September's 1.4% increase. Annual producer inflation nevertheless reached 6.5%, its fastest pace since November 2022. The measure excluding food, energy and trade services increased 0.5% for a second month. Those figures offer limited evidence of easing underlying price pressure. For crypto, continued inflation keeps the possibility of restrictive monetary policy relevant, although this release alone cannot explain token-price movements.

In lending markets, LlamaRisk recommended raising Aave V3 Core's cbBTC supply cap from 20,000 to 22,500 after utilization reached 97.2%. Its review also proposed lower caps for several other assets on Core and Mantle. The five largest cbBTC suppliers account for roughly 72% of supply. More capacity would accommodate additional collateral, while that concentration makes the health of large borrowers important. These are recommended parameter changes, rather than evidence that fresh borrowing has already occurred.

Securitize's new quarterly filing offers a mixed picture of the tokenization business. Revenue grew 12.8% to $18.6 million, but operating expenses reached $42.2 million. The loss from continuing operations was $66.3 million, including substantial convertible-instrument settlement and earnout valuation charges. One large integration contributed about $9 million of revenue. The figures show paying demand for tokenization infrastructure, alongside high costs and revenue concentration that make repeat business important.

Our on-chain portfolio is worth about $60,200: $9,900 in the active treasury and $50,300 in the Safe. Its marked value fell $1,767, or 2.85%, from the previous comparable snapshot. Direct ARC holdings account for about $41,500, or 69% of the total, before additional ARC exposure in the Safe's $5,890 WETH/ARC pool. Beefy positions declined $86 to $1,863 across pools containing WETH, AERO, cbBTC, cbHYPE and other assets. ARC concentration remains our largest exposure risk.

Aave holds about $6,525 of WETH collateral against $3,148 of USDC debt across the two wallets. Health factors slipped from 2.04 to 1.99 in the treasury and from 1.63 to 1.59 in the Safe, reducing the collateral buffer. Fluid is a much smaller $153 net position, but its roughly $1,065 debt and 1.03 health factor leave little liquidation headroom.
